assignments.evidence: Always 'NAME sutufako' right after the deceased's name and before 'NAME girisfako' (begotten by father): the mother's filiation slot (491 times).
Given with gukhira like zohu (beer), never poured; it also turns up in livestock and offering lists: bread with beer.
Poured with pafora like sezi (water), never given; also in temple offering lists, so it is the second liquid besides water and beer.
Counted livestock: 'folofu 2 ne 3 miyu 100', 'folofudu 568 ma nedu 165 sapezo' (took oxen and cows), and nedu in dedications.
Ends every adoration text: 'items ... yubi/wutibi dultuzo', meaning he offered them to the temple or the wuti.
The only title that takes god names as its -ne complement ('haltuto sune/fupurne/yane NAME'); it is twice as frequent as the other titles.
In the annals, 'X-bi seyozo duwodu/fefukradu/kunalirdu resdozo' is followed by captives taken and men killed: went to X and seized it.
'fupurne yumu dapukzo lurufo 47 gukhizo': the temple of the god, built, then gold given; it always takes yu (temple).
Royal epithet 'monharzas RNAME fupurne/sune dozezo': the king whom the god loved.
Only in 'dultuzo wepakne togulra' after an offering, meaning may the god protect his life.
'yowidu N fokladu N (pasodu N) hizadu sapezo': it never carries a number and closes the people list, so it means taken as captives.
Comes first in the captive head-count list and is the only one killed ('yowidu wakizo', 12 times).
Always the second counted group of captives, after yowi, with large numbers.
An optional third captive group with small counts (17 to 89), after men and women.
Alternates with yu (temple) as the place offerings go to ('wutibi dultuzo'), so it is the house of the god.
The commonest kin slot word ('NAME zufako', about twice any other kin term) yet never used in the 'NAME X-fako NAME' labels, so it is the generic relation.
The default offering adjective ('sezi/wu/kikrira/zohu gun pafora/gukhira'), twice as frequent as zura or suse (good).
The other offering adjective beside suse (good) and gun, used evenly on water, milk, bread and beer: pure offerings.
Only in the personal epithet slot 'pirafako' after the kin list, alternating with 'susefako' (good); never on offerings.
Kin term; the most frequent in the short 'NAME X-fako NAME' labels (16, against pizu 12 and zitomu or galu 8), which suits 'wife of'.
Seized in the annals ('kunalirdu resdozo') and also a generic affiliation beside yu and city names ('gewu/haltuto kunalirne NAME').
Only as an annals object: 'X-bi seyozo duwodu resdozo' (seized after going to X); land or boat is a coin flip with fefukra.
Only as an annals object: 'X-bi seyozo fefukradu resdozo'; never an affiliation, so boat or land; a coin flip with duwo.
Kin term in 'NAME zitomufako' and in labels; spread just like galu, so brother or sister is a guess.
Kin term in 'NAME galufako' and in labels; spread just like zitomu, so brother or sister is a guess.
Official title ('NAME gewu', 'gewu place-ne NAME', dedicant); slightly the most often 'of the temple' (yune); otherwise spread like fakmu and hil.
Official title of a place ('fakmu hekdone NAME'), dedicant in adorations; spread just like gewu and hil.
Official title of a place ('hil yukane NAME'), dedicant in adorations; spread just like gewu and fakmu.
